weights.csoNote: Under-diagnosed in Uganda (limited CTPA/D-dimer) — basePrior reflects detection, not true incidence which is likely higher. Confirm with CSO.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2019 Acute Pulmonary Embolism Guidelines (Konstantinides SV et al., Eur Heart J 2020;41:543-603)

weights.csoNote: Uganda: TB can cause secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. Tension = tracheal deviation + hyperresonance + absent breath sounds + haemodynamic compromise -> immediate decompression.
weights.weightCitation: Macleod's Clinical Examination 15th ed (2023); Davidson's 24th ed; BTS Pleural Disease Guideline (2023)

weights.csoNote: Uganda: rheumatic, hypertensive, peripartum and HIV cardiomyopathy are common causes — Ugandan HF is often YOUNGER than Western HF. Cardiac wheeze ('cardiac asthma') can mimic airways disease.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2021 Heart Failure Guidelines (McDonagh TA et al., Eur Heart J 2021;42:3599-3726) + 2023 focused update; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Life-threatening features (silent chest, exhaustion, cyanosis, poor respiratory effort) escalate to emergency — a 'silent chest' is more ominous than loud wheeze.
weights.weightCitation: GINA 2025 (asthma); GOLD 2025 Report (COPD) — verify current version at build; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: in HIV consider bacterial pneumonia, PCP and TB in the same differential.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (pneumonia); WHO; Surviving Sepsis Campaign; Davidson's 24th ed; BTS CAP guideline

weights.csoNote: Uganda: anaemia very common — malaria, sickle cell, hookworm/iron deficiency, HIV, nutritional. NOTE: SpO2 can read NORMAL despite inadequate oxygen-carrying capacity; severe anaemia is a danger sign needing transfusion access.
weights.weightCitation: WHO guidance on anaemia; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION — the engine must not anchor here before excluding PE, asthma/COPD, metabolic acidosis and cardiac causes. Also: 'depression/anxiety' is not in the risk capture token set (used here but flagged as a gap to add).

Uganda: TB is the LEADING cause of exudative pleural effusion; also parapneumonic/empyema and malignant. Exam: stony dullness + reduced breath sounds + reduced vocal resonance; diagnostic aspiration (Light's criteria) is key.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB; Uganda National TB & Leprosy Programme; Davidson's 24th ed; BTS Pleural Disease Guideline 2023 (Light's criteria)

weights.csoNote: The cardinal sign (KUSSMAUL deep/sighing breathing) is NOT in the capture token set — polyuria/polydipsia + the diabetes/CKD context are the capturable proxies. Because NEW-ONSET DKA may not yet carry a diabetes label, the conditional pin also fires on the polyuria/polydipsia feature. SAFEST: always prompt a capillary-glucose check in any breathless/unwell patient (DEFG — Don't Ever Forget Glucose) regardless of the pin. Confirm with CSO.
weights.weightCitation: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS Consensus on Hyperglycaemic Crises (DKA/HHS), Diabetes Care 2024; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Ugandan causes differ — schistosomiasis-associated PAH and POST-TB lung disease are important, alongside HIV-PAH and mitral stenosis (RHD). Schistosomiasis exposure is NOT in the risk capture token set (gap to add). Chronic progressive exertional dyspnoea +/- right-heart-failure signs.
weights.weightCitation: ESC/ERS 2022 Pulmonary Hypertension Guidelines (Humbert M et al., Eur Heart J 2022;43:3618-3731); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: TB pericarditis (often HIV-co-infected) is a leading cause of large pericardial effusion and tamponade — treatable but lethal if missed. Cardinal tamponade signs (raised JVP, muffled heart sounds, pulsus paradoxus, hypotension) are EXAMINATION findings NOT in the feature token set — echocardiography is diagnostic. Confirm scope/weighting with CSO.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2015 Pericardial Diseases Guidelines (Adler Y et al., Eur Heart J 2015;36:2921-2964); IMPI trial (Mayosi BM, African TB pericarditis); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss — pin only when HIV/immunosuppression present (advanced HIV, CD4<200). basePrior population-dependent. Hallmark: subacute progressive EXERTIONAL dyspnoea + dry cough + marked desaturation ON EXERTION disproportionate to CXR/examination.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines on HIV-related opportunistic infections; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed (PCP — advanced HIV, CD4<200)

weights.csoNote: Uganda: post-TB lung disease (bronchiectasis, fibrosis, airflow obstruction, destroyed lung) is a MAJOR cause of chronic breathlessness given the TB burden; may develop secondary pulmonary hypertension/cor pulmonale and aspergilloma in residual cavities.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; WHO post-TB lung health framework; BTS (post-TB lung disease)

weights.csoNote: Airway EMERGENCY, but the cardinal sign — STRIDOR — is NOT in the feature token set and must be distinguished from wheeze (stridor = upper airway/inspiratory; wheeze = lower airway/expiratory). Recommend adding a 'stridor' sign token. Causes span anaphylaxis, foreign body, epiglottitis, retropharyngeal/Ludwig's angina, and laryngeal/thyroid tumour. A suspected case needs immediate airway assessment, not routine workup.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; Macleod's Clinical Examination 15th ed (2023) (upper-airway obstruction — stridor, airway emergency)
